video.title: You Were Lied To. THIS Is How You Actually Get Rich In America

summary: David Heacock argues that the traditional American Dream path of college, a prestigious job, home ownership, and retirement is less reliable than it used to be. He describes leaving Goldman Sachs to buy his family’s industrial supply business and building Filterbuy around the shipping economics of air filters. He recommends building skills society will pay for, with HVAC work as an example of a path from apprenticeship to business ownership and a possible sale. His broader advice is to choose a life before choosing a business, protect your options from debt, and take responsibility for learning and creating value.

tactics.name: Choose a product with a structural domestic advantage
steps: Look at the physical characteristics of a product and its shipping costs relative to its price.
Compare the product's logistics needs with the geography of the market.
Choose a product where domestic production and local presence can be an advantage.

quote.text: Air filters have a very specific characteristic. They're bulky and they're cheap relative to what it cost to ship them.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Build an HVAC business from a trade skill
steps: Train and work as an HVAC technician at an established company.
Move into 1099 work, run a crew, and take installation jobs.
Build a brand, customer base, and book of business.
If growth is desired, expand into neighboring cities or buy businesses in the same trade from owners who want to exit.

quote.text: Step two is you go 1099. You run your own crew and you start taking installation jobs.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Choose a paid skill before taking on education debt
steps: Ask what work the degree or training enables you to do.
Check whether someone will pay for that work.
If you cannot identify paid work at the end, do not sign the loan.

quote.text: At the end of this, what can I do that somebody will pay me for? If you can't answer it, don't sign the loan.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Set a life goal before selecting a business
steps: Decide what you want your life to look like.
Choose a business or career that can support that life.
Keep learning and adjust as the economy and customer value change.

quote.text: Decide what you actually want your life to look like before you pick the business, not after.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Look for structural advantages in the product and its logistics rather than choosing a business only because of personal passion.

quote.text: Don't ask what you're passionate about, ask where you have a structural advantage nobody can undo with cheaper labor.

lessons.lesson: A trade can provide a paid skill and a path into ownership without requiring a degree or business debt.
